sentences.en: My colleague Natalie Kicherev talked to White House reporter Peter Baker about what to expect this time.
sentences.zh: 我的同事娜塔莉·基奇雷夫采访了白宫记者彼得·贝克，谈谈这次我们应该期待什么。

sentences.zh: 今天是 10 月 1 日，星期二。

sentences.en: Peter, walk us through the extraordinary circumstances of the only time a president facing impeachment left office under pressure from his own party, Richard Nixon.
sentences.zh: 彼得，请为我们梳理一下那些不同寻常的情况：唯一一次面临弹劾的总统在来自本党施压下离职，也就是理查德·尼克松。

sentences.en: I refer, of course, to the investigations of the so-called Watergate affair.
sentences.zh: 我指的当然是对所谓“水门事件”的调查。

sentences.en: Well, this, of course, was two years into Watergate.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这当然发生在水门事件爆发两年后。

sentences.en: There have been investigations for many, many months.
sentences.zh: 调查已经进行了好几个月。

sentences.en: I believe the time has come to bring that investigation and the other investigations of this matter to an end.
sentences.zh: 我相信是时候结束对这件事以及其他事项的调查了。

sentences.en: One year of Watergate is good enough.
sentences.zh: 水门事件闹了一年已经够了。

sentences.en: And Nixon had basically survived it up until this point, and Republicans largely stayed with him.
sentences.zh: 尼克松基本上一直挺到了这个时候，共和党人也大体上支持他。

sentences.en: What really finally did him in, what finally put things over the edge, was something they called the smoking gun tape.
sentences.zh: 真正最终击垮他、让局势彻底翻转的，被称为“确凿的录音证据”。

sentences.en: What did the president know, and when did he know it?
sentences.zh: 总统知道了什么？又是什么时候知道的？

sentences.en: On July 16th, Alexander
sentences.zh: 7 月 16 日，亚历山大·

sentences.en: Butterfield, a former White House official, shocked the Senate Watergate committee by saying the president's conversations were on tape.
sentences.zh: 巴特菲尔德，一位前白宫官员，向参议院水门事件委员会透露了一个令人震惊的消息：总统的对话都被录音了。

sentences.en: And this particular tape of a conversation showed that Nixon, in fact, had ordered his aides to tell the CIA to block the FBI investigation into Watergate.
sentences.zh: 而这段特定的对话录音显示，尼克松实际上曾下令其助手告诉中情局去阻止联邦调查局对水门事件的调查。

sentences.en: In other words, he had directly ordered the cover-up.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，他直接下令进行掩盖。

sentences.en: That was the bridge too far.
sentences.zh: 那是越过底线的行为。

sentences.en: For the Republicans, that was the final straw.
sentences.zh: 对共和党人来说，那是压垮骆驼的最后一根稻草。

sentences.en: Congressman Rhodes and Senator Scott and I have just concluded a visit with the president.
sentences.zh: 众议员罗兹、参议员斯科特和我刚刚结束了对总统的拜访。

sentences.en: There's this dramatic moment when three senior Republicans from Congress, Barry Goldwater,
sentences.zh: 有一个戏剧性的时刻，国会的三位资深共和党人——巴里·戈德水

sentences.en: John Rose, Hugh Scott, they come to the White House and they tell Nixon.
sentences.zh: 约翰·罗兹、休·斯科特——他们来到白宫告诉尼克松。

sentences.en: We have told him that the situation is very gloomy on Capitol Hill, and that it is a very distressing situation.
sentences.zh: 我们已经告诉他，国会山的形势非常严峻，情况令人极为担忧。

sentences.en: It's over.
sentences.zh: 一切都结束了。

sentences.en: The time is up.
sentences.zh: 时间到了。

sentences.en: He no longer has enough support to survive.
sentences.zh: 他不再拥有足够的支持来度过难关。

sentences.en: That he's not only going to be impeached by the House, but convicted by the Senate.
sentences.zh: 他不仅会被众议院弹劾，还会在参议院被定罪。

sentences.en: He probably only has 10 Republican senators who are still willing to stand with him.
sentences.zh: 他可能只剩下 10 名参议员还愿意支持他。

sentences.en: That's when they abandoned him.
sentences.zh: 正是在那个时候，他们抛弃了他。

sentences.en: And it's only at that point did they abandon him.
sentences.zh: 而且只有在这个时候，他们才抛弃了他。

sentences.en: I shall resign the presidency, effective at noon tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 我将辞去总统职务，于明天中午生效。

sentences.en: Which, of course, prompted him to resign.
sentences.zh: 这当然促使他宣布辞职。

sentences.en: Rather than face the humiliation of impeachment and conviction by the Senate, he would short-circuit the process, in effect, by saying, I give up.
sentences.zh: 与其面对被众议院弹劾和参议院定罪的羞辱，他不如通过表态“我放弃了、我不干了”来变相中止这个进程。

sentences.en: I'm out of here.
sentences.zh: 我这就离开。

sentences.en: To continue to fight through the months ahead for my personal vindication would almost totally absorb the time and attention of both the president and the Congress.
sentences.zh: 在未来几个月里继续为恢复我的个人清白而战，将几乎完全占用总统和国会的时间与精力。

sentences.en: So, obviously, there's a lot of similarities to that moment and the one we're in now.
sentences.zh: 所以，很显然，那一刻与我们现在的处境有很多相似之处。

sentences.en: You could argue that we have the proverbial smoking gun with the transcript that the White House itself released last week of Trump's call with the president of Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 你可以认为，白宫上周自己公布的特朗普与乌克兰总统通话的文字记录，就是我们常说的确凿证据。

sentences.en: So why doesn't it seem like the same thing is happening now?
sentences.zh: 那么，为什么现在看起来没有发生同样的事情呢？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: In fact, you heard House Democrats, when they read that rough transcript of the phone call, say it was a smoking gun.
sentences.zh: 事实上，你听到众议院民主党人在阅读那份通话的粗略文字记录时，说这就是确凿证据。

sentences.en: They used that term, smoking gun.
sentences.zh: 他们用了这个词，确凿证据。

sentences.en: That is the smoking gun.

sentences.en: I personally think that that document is the smoking gun.

sentences.en: We should not be trying to find a secret smoking gun.

sentences.zh: 你听不到的是许多共和党人这么说。

sentences.en: This was a normal conversation between two leaders, and we've got the president of Ukraine saying there was no pressure.
sentences.zh: 这是两位领导人之间的一次正常对话，而且我们有乌克兰总统说其中没有施压。

sentences.en: Most of the Republicans said, no, I don't think this tells us enough about the president's interactions with Ukraine to suggest it was somehow nefarious.
sentences.zh: 大多数共和党人说，不，我不认为这让我们对总统与乌克兰的互动了解得足够多，以至于暗示它有什么不可告人的目的。

sentences.en: He simply made a request that the Ukrainians investigate corruption.
sentences.zh: 他只是提出了一个请求，希望乌克兰人调查腐败。

sentences.en: There's no quid pro quo.
sentences.zh: 这里没有利益交换。

sentences.en: No talk about aid.
sentences.zh: 没有谈到援助。

sentences.en: No quid pro quo.
sentences.zh: 没有利益交换。

sentences.en: The Democrat chairman themselves has said there was no quid pro quo here.
sentences.zh: 民主党主席自己也说过，这里没有利益交换。

sentences.en: Quid pro quo, of course, would be, if you do this, I'll do that.
sentences.zh: 利益交换，当然就是指“如果你做了这个，我就做那个”。

sentences.en: But since he didn't, he said that there's nothing there to call high crime a misdemeanor.

sentences.zh: 你怎么看待这段交流？

sentences.zh: 而凯文·

sentences.zh: 麦卡锡并不知道“不过”这个词已经在里面了，当然也没有把它当成什么特别有意义的证据死死抓住不放。

sentences.en: The difference here is that the smoking gun is not quite as smoking as it was in the case of
sentences.zh: 这里的区别在于，现在的确凿证据不像当年尼克松

sentences.en: Nixon.
sentences.zh: 事件中那样确凿。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全如此。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全如此。

sentences.en: That anyway, it hasn't been seen by both parties in the same way that the smoking gun tape was seen in 1974.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，两党对它的看法不像 1974 年对待水门事件录音那样一致。

sentences.en: So how does President Trump's approach to all of this compare to Nixon's?
sentences.zh: 那么，特朗普总统处理这一切的方式与尼克松相比如何？

sentences.zh: 当 1974 年确凿的录音带曝光时，尼克松领会了暗示。

sentences.en: Rather than face the humiliation of impeachment and conviction by the Senate, he would short circuit the process in effect by saying, I give up.
sentences.zh: 与其面对被参议院弹劾和定罪的羞辱，他不如通过表态“我放弃了、我不干了”来变相中止这个进程。

sentences.en: I'm out of here.
sentences.zh: 我这就离开。

sentences.zh: 25 年后，当比尔·克林顿面临弹劾时……

sentences.en: I did not have sexual relations with that woman, Ms. Lewinsky.
sentences.zh: 我没有和那个女人发生性关系，莱温斯基女士。

sentences.en: I never told anybody to lie.
sentences.zh: 我从未叫任何人撒谎。

sentences.en: Not a single time.
sentences.zh: 一次也没有。

sentences.en: Never.

sentences.en: He absolutely refused to resign.
sentences.zh: 他绝对拒绝辞职。

sentences.en: A lot of Democrats would have liked him to.
sentences.zh: 很多民主党人其实希望他辞职。

sentences.en: They were very unhappy with what he had done.
sentences.zh: 他们对他的所作所为非常不满。

sentences.en: They thought he had brought shame to the office and had damaged the party.
sentences.zh: 他们认为他给这个职位带来了耻辱，并损害了党派的利益。

sentences.en: I will continue to do the work of the American people.
sentences.zh: 我将继续为美国人民的工作而努力。

sentences.en: We still, after all, have to save Social
sentences.zh: 毕竟，我们仍然必须为 21 世纪拯救社会

sentences.en: Security and Medicare for the 21st century.
sentences.zh: 保障和医疗保险。

sentences.en: But Clinton showed something different.
sentences.zh: 但克林顿展现了完全不同的一面。

sentences.en: He showed that if you just simply stick it out, if you simply aren't ashamed, if you don't let embarrassment or ridicule or constant battering
sentences.zh: 他表明，只要你坚持下去，只要你毫不羞耻，只要你不让尴尬、嘲笑或持续的抨击

sentences.en: drive you out, that you can probably bluff your way into holding on to office.
sentences.zh: 把你赶走，你很可能就能虚张声势地保住职位。

sentences.en: I have accepted responsibility for what I did wrong in my personal life.
sentences.zh: 我已经为我在个人生活中所做错的事情承担了责任。

sentences.en: The question is, what are we going to do now?
sentences.zh: 问题是，我们现在要做什么？

sentences.en: And Clinton said basically to Congress, I dare you.
sentences.zh: 克林顿基本上是在向国会叫板：我借你个胆子。

sentences.en: Try to take me down because you can't.
sentences.zh: 试着把我搞垮，因为你们做不到。

sentences.en: So if you're Trump and you're looking at that history, there's a strong case for following

sentences.en: Yeah, that's exactly right.

sentences.en: In fact, you know, I wrote a book about Clinton's impeachment called The Breach.
sentences.zh: 事实上，你知道，我写过一本关于克林顿弹劾案的书，名叫《决裂》（The Breach）。

sentences.en: And while I was doing the research for it, I interviewed a couple
sentences.zh: 在做相关研究时，我采访了几位

sentences.zh: 在调查水门事件中起过关键作用的共和党人，担任参议员的霍华德·贝克，以及担任共和党法律顾问的弗雷德·汤普森。

sentences.en: And both of them told me in separate interviews something I was really struck by.
sentences.zh: 他们在各自的采访中都告诉我一件事，让我印象极其深刻。

sentences.en: And I think that shows you how much had changed since the 1970s in terms of our politics, and particularly the politics of impeachment.
sentences.zh: 我认为这向你表明，自 20 世纪 70 年代以来，我们的政治，特别是弹劾政治，已经发生了多么巨大的变化。

sentences.zh: 彼得，我觉得值得指出的是，你所指出的这一点是，国会程序在弹劾期间其实从未真正罢免过总统。

sentences.en: We think of the Nixon story as an example of bipartisan action on this, but it wasn't quite that.
sentences.zh: 我们把尼克松的故事看作是两党对此采取一致行动的例子，但事实并非完全如此。

sentences.en: That's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: In the end, Nixon gave up.
sentences.zh: 到头来，尼克松放弃了。

sentences.en: And the question is whether in today's political environment, whether there could ever be a moment where a two-thirds majority in the Senate
sentences.zh: 问题在于，在当今的政治环境下，是否会出现这样一个时刻：参议院中必须由两党成员组成的三分之二多数

sentences.en: that would have to compose members of both parties would ever agree to remove a president.
sentences.zh: 会同意罢免一位总统？

sentences.zh: 无论如何，到目前为止，美国公众一直对弹劾

sentences.zh: 特朗普总统不感兴趣。

sentences.en: That may be beginning to change.
sentences.zh: 这种情况可能开始发生变化了。

sentences.en: CBS, in fact, over the weekend, they found that 55 percent of Americans now support an impeachment inquiry.
sentences.zh: 事实上，哥伦比亚广播公司（CBS）在周末发现，55% 的美国人现在支持进行弹劾调查。

sentences.en: And that's the first time a majority of Americans have done that.
sentences.zh: 这是多数美国人首次这样做。

sentences.en: So that changed the dynamics a little bit.
sentences.zh: 所以这稍微改变了态势。

sentences.en: But if you're a Republican, the more important number is probably the number of Republicans who support the president at this
sentences.zh: 但如果你是一个共和党人，更重要的数字可能是目前支持总统的共和党人比例，

sentences.en: point, which is still in the 80 to 90 percent range in most polls.
sentences.zh: 在大多数民调中，这一比例仍然在 80% 到 90% 之间。

sentences.en: In other words, the president is still very popular with Republican core voters.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，这位总统在共和党核心选民中依然非常受欢迎。

sentences.en: So what you're saying is it might not matter to Republicans that much that the broader public opinion has shifted toward favoring an impeachment inquiry.
sentences.zh: 所以你的意思是，对于共和党人来说，更广泛的公众舆论转向赞成弹劾调查，可能并没有那么重要。

sentences.en: It's not the most important thing.
sentences.zh: 这不是最重要的事情。

sentences.en: I mean, it was change in the last 20 years since the Clinton impeachment, the last 40 some years since the Nixon impeachment, is the parties have really
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在克林顿遭弹劾后的过去20年里，在尼克松遭弹劾后的过去40多年里，发生的变化是，两党真的

sentences.en: become more and more homogenized so that there really are just conservatives in the Republican
sentences.zh: 变得越来越同质化，以至于共和党内

sentences.en: Party and just liberals in the Democratic Party and not a lot of people in the middle anymore.
sentences.zh: 真的只有保守派，民主党内只有自由派，中间派已经不多了。

sentences.en: And they're running in districts where the greater threat is that you lose your seat to somebody on your flank, not that you lose swing voters in the middle.
sentences.zh: 而且他们竞选的选区，更大的威胁是你会在党内激进派的挑战中失去席位，而不是在中间选区失去摇摆选民。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So if you're a Republican, you're more concerned that you lose the support of conservatives than you do that you lose the support of independents or moderates.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你是共和党人，比起失去独立选民或温和派的支持，你更担心失去保守派的支持。

sentences.en: And that means that your incentive structure is to stay with a president who is popular with the core voters.
sentences.zh: 这意味着你的激励机制是留在一个深受核心选民欢迎的总统身边。

sentences.en: Can you think of a single Republican senator who seems likely to break from the party in this moment?
sentences.zh: 你能想出一个在这个时候似乎有可能背离党的共和党参议员吗？

sentences.en: I think you can imagine a scenario if the House were to impeach and if there continued to be some revelations that were damaging to the president in which a handful of Republican
sentences.zh: 我想你可以想象这样一种情况：如果众议院发起弹劾，并且不断出现对总统不利的新爆料，那么少数共和党

sentences.en: senators might vote against the president.
sentences.zh: 参议员可能会投票反对总统。

sentences.en: I did read the transcript.
sentences.zh: 我确实读了文字记录。

sentences.en: You know,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，

sentences.en: Mitt Romney has expressed his concern over what's happening with Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 米特·罗姆尼已经对乌克兰发生的事件表达了他的担忧。

sentences.en: It remains troubling in the extreme.
sentences.zh: 这极其令人不安。

sentences.en: It's deeply troubling.
sentences.zh: 这深感令人不安。

sentences.en: Senator Ben Sasse has said, quote,
sentences.zh: 参议员本·萨斯曾说，引述如下：

sentences.en: Republicans ought not be rushing to circle the wagons and say there's no there there when there's obviously a lot that's very troubling there.
sentences.zh: 共和党人不应该急于抱团辩护，在明明有很多非常令人不安的事情时却说那里什么也没有。

sentences.en: This stuff is troubling.
sentences.zh: 这些事情确实令人不安。

sentences.en: I don't think either one of them is at the moment ready to declare that they would be for removal from office.
sentences.zh: 我不认为他们两人目前准备宣布他们会支持将其罢免。

sentences.en: But a handful of them at least would be potentially open to that possibility if the fact set presented itself.
sentences.zh: 但如果有相关事实摆在眼前，他们中至少有一部分人可能对这种可能性持开放态度。

sentences.en: It's hard to see 20.
sentences.zh: 很难凑够20人。

sentences.en: And why is that number relevant?
sentences.zh: 为什么这个数字很重要？

sentences.en: Well, let's let's just remember how impeachment works, of course.
sentences.zh: 好吧，让我们回想一下弹劾是如何运作的。

sentences.en: Impeachment starts in the House of Representatives and it requires a majority of members of the House to vote to impeach the president for high crimes and misdemeanors.
sentences.zh: 弹劾始于众议院，需要众议院多数成员投票通过，以严重罪行和轻罪弹劾总统。

sentences.en: Now, that's like an indictment.
sentences.zh: 这就像是一场起诉。

sentences.en: It's a charge, in effect, that the president has committed crimes against the republic, if you will.
sentences.zh: 实际上，这是一种指控，认为总统犯下了背叛共和国的罪行，如果你愿意这么说的话。

sentences.en: If the House majority were to pass an impeachment article against the president, it then goes to the Senate.
sentences.zh: 如果众议院多数派通过了针对总统的弹劾条款，它就会移交给参议院。

sentences.en: The Senate would then, in theory, put the president on trial.
sentences.zh: 然后，按理论讲，参议院将对总统进行审判。

sentences.en: The trial would, if the Clinton precedent were to hold, bring members of the House over who had voted to impeach the president.
sentences.zh: 如果参照克林顿先例，审判将把曾投票弹劾总统的众议院议员带到参议院。

sentences.en: William Jefferson Clinton has committed high crimes and misdemeanors.
sentences.zh: 威廉·杰斐逊·克林顿犯下了严重罪行和轻罪。

sentences.en: Convict him and remove him.
sentences.zh: 定罪并罢免他。

sentences.en: To serve as prosecutors, if you will.
sentences.zh: 担任检察官，如果你愿意这样称呼的话。

sentences.en: They call them managers.
sentences.zh: 他们称之为诉讼管理人。

sentences.en: Impeachment is about restoring honor and integrity to the office.
sentences.zh: 弹劾是为了恢复该职位的荣誉和正直。

sentences.en: And then the president would be entitled to bring lawyers of his own to the Senate floor to defend him.
sentences.zh: 然后总统将有权带他自己的律师来到参议院大厅为他辩护。

sentences.en: We're here today because the president suffered a terrible moral lapse, a marital infidelity, not a breach of the public trust, not a crime against society.
sentences.zh: 我们今天在这里，是因为总统遭受了严重的道德失范，这是婚姻不忠，而不是背叛公众信任，也不是对社会犯罪。

sentences.en: And then the evidence would be presented and the Senate would vote.
sentences.zh: 然后将出示证据，参议院将进行投票。

sentences.en: Now, to actually convict the president and remove him from office would require a two-thirds vote.
sentences.zh: 要真正给总统定罪并将他免职，需要三分之二的投票。

sentences.en: Now, in this Senate, that would mean 67 votes.
sentences.zh: 在目前的参议院中，这意味着67票。

sentences.en: Because there are, in fact, only 47 Democrats, that means you need at least 20 Republican senators to vote to convict.
sentences.zh: 因为事实上只有47名民主党人，这意味着你需要至少20名共和党参议员投票赞成定罪。

sentences.en: Otherwise, the president would be acquitted and he would remain in office for the rest of his term.
sentences.zh: 否则，总统将被宣告无罪，并将在其任期内继续留任。

sentences.en: And, Peter, do we know for sure that Mitch McConnell is going to have a trial?
sentences.zh: 彼得，我们能确定米奇·麦康奈尔一定会进行审判吗？

sentences.en: Well, it's a great question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很好的问题。

sentences.en: People have been asking over the last few days because, you know, he, of course, didn't have a vote on Merrick Garland's Supreme Court nomination in
sentences.zh: 过去几天人们一直在问，因为你知道，他当然没有对梅里克·加兰在
2016年的最高法院提名进行投票。

sentences.en: So a lot of people say, well, maybe he would just simply declare that he wouldn't take it up.
sentences.zh: 所以很多人说，好吧，也许他会直接宣布他不会审理此案。

sentences.en: But he actually just said on Monday, I would have no choice but to take it up.
sentences.zh: 但他周一实际上刚说过，我别无选择，只能审理。

sentences.en: How long you're on it is a whole different matter.
sentences.zh: 你在上面花多长时间完全是另一回事。

sentences.en: But I would have no choice but to take it up based on a Senate rule on impeachment.
sentences.zh: 但根据参议院关于弹劾的规则，我别无选择，只能审理。

sentences.en: The Constitution doesn't require him to take it up.
sentences.zh: 宪法没有要求他必须审理。

sentences.en: The Constitution says the Senate has the power to try a president.
sentences.zh: 宪法规定参议院有权审判总统。

sentences.en: But the Senate rules do specifically say that if the House impeaches a president, that the Senate must take it up the very next day.
sentences.zh: 但参议院规则确实明确规定，如果众议院弹劾总统，参议院必须在第二天进行审理。

sentences.en: Now, what kind of trial it would be, we don't know.
sentences.zh: 至于会是一场什么样的审判，我们还不知道。

sentences.en: You could open the trial and then a supporter of the president's or even Mitch McConnell himself could introduce a motion to dismiss the case on the basis that there
sentences.zh: 你可以开启审判，然后总统的支持者甚至米奇·麦康奈尔本人都可以提出动议，以

sentences.en: is no evidence or not enough evidence or that that doesn't seem likely to get to a two-thirds vote.
sentences.zh: 没有证据、证据不足或似乎不太可能达到三分之二多数票为由驳回此案。

sentences.en: So why bother to belabor the process?
sentences.zh: 那为什么还要费劲纠缠这个程序呢？

sentences.en: You could have this motion to dismiss and then that could be passed by a majority of the Senate.
sentences.zh: 你可以提出这项驳回动议，然后参议院多数票通过即可。

sentences.en: And then, in fact, the trial would be over.
sentences.zh: 事实上，审判就会这样结束。

sentences.en: They tried this during the Clinton case.
sentences.zh: 他们在克林顿案中尝试过这一点。

sentences.en: It didn't work.
sentences.zh: 没有成功。

sentences.en: So there is some precedent for it.
sentences.zh: 所以这确实有一些先例。

sentences.en: The truth is there have only been two Senate trials of a president in our history, one in 1868, one in 1999.
sentences.zh: 事实是，在我们历史上一共只有过两次对总统的参议院审判，一次在1868年，一次在1999年。

sentences.en: Both times they kind of made it up as they went along because there is no rule book for this.
sentences.zh: 这两次他们都是走一步算一步，因为根本没有针对这个的规章手册。

sentences.en: So you can imagine that we will be making it up as we go along all over again.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以想象，我们将再次走一步算一步。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 纽约时报应用？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 已解锁？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 众所周知，你需要订阅《时报》才能访问所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但是，如果你能免费探索《时报》一个月，且无需输入信用卡呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你首次下载纽约时报应用程序时，你在应用中的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 有一个月的时间突破付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么内容。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载时报应用并获得30天免费访问权限。

sentences.en: So McConnell is indicating that he's willing to hold this Senate trial, but we don't know exactly how it's going to go down.
sentences.zh: 所以麦康奈尔暗示他愿意举行这场参议院审判，但我们不知道具体会如何发展。

sentences.en: And in any case, all signs are pointing to the Senate acquitting Trump.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，所有迹象都表明参议院会判决特朗普无罪。

sentences.en: Right, exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错，完全如此。

sentences.en: Something drastic would have to change, presumably, like, for instance, the economy going bad, the president's poll numbers going south in a serious way, not just across the board,
sentences.zh: 据推测，必须发生一些急剧的变化，比如，经济恶化，总统的支持率严重下滑，不仅是全面下滑，

sentences.en: but also with Republicans.
sentences.zh: 而且在共和党人当中也是如此。

sentences.en: Things like that would probably have to happen in order to see such a drastic defection from the Republican caucus in the Senate.
sentences.zh: 可能必须发生类似的事情，才能看到参议院共和党党团出现如此剧烈的倒戈。

sentences.en: So given those dynamics, what is the GOP's strategy for talking about this phone call and the whistleblower's allegations to voters?
sentences.zh: 鉴于这些动态，共和党向选民谈论这通电话和举报人指控的策略是什么？

sentences.en: Well, one thing they're trying to do is to make it out as if this is strictly a radical effort by disgruntled Democrats who never got over losing the 2016 election.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们试图做的一件事是，把它说成是一场彻头彻尾的激进努力，是由那些对2016年大选失利耿耿于怀的不满的民主党人发起的。

sentences.en: They're angry about the 2016 election, and ultimately, they're angry at the voters.
sentences.zh: 他们对2016年大选感到愤怒，归根结底，他们对选民感到愤怒。

sentences.en: They're angry that the voters elected President Trump.
sentences.zh: 他们对选民选举了特朗普总统感到愤怒。

sentences.en: All of this from day one.
sentences.zh: 从第一天起就是这样。

sentences.en: From day one, they have been wanting to get this president out of office.
sentences.zh: 从第一天起，他们就一直想让这位总统下台。

sentences.en: To, in effect, have a coup d'etat against President Trump.
sentences.zh: 实际上，就是对特朗普总统发动一场政变。

sentences.en: You see email after email, attack after attack on individual Democrats from supporting an impeachment inquiry.
sentences.zh: 你会看到一封又一封的电子邮件，一次又一次对支持弹劾调查的个别民主党人的攻击。

sentences.en: Her extreme left is angry.
sentences.zh: 她那边的极左翼很愤怒。

sentences.en: They're marching in the street with pitchforks and torches.
sentences.zh: 他们拿着草叉和火把走上街头。

sentences.en: Congresswoman so-and-so has given into the radical socialist left of her party.
sentences.zh: 某某女议员向她党内的激进社会主义左翼妥协了。

sentences.en: Your congressman so-and-so is just part of a mob attack on the president.
sentences.zh: 你们的某某国会议员只是针对总统的暴民攻击的一部分。

sentences.en: So they're trying to turn it on the
sentences.zh: 所以他们试图把矛头指向

sentences.en: Democrats.
sentences.zh: 民主党人。

sentences.en: They also, of course, want to focus on Joe Biden.
sentences.zh: 当然，他们也想把焦点放在乔·拜登身上。

sentences.en: Everywhere Joe Biden goes, his son follows and gets millions of dollars from the government.
sentences.zh: 乔·拜登走到哪里，他的儿子就跟到哪里，并从政府获得数百万美元。

sentences.en: The president is right to ask for an investigation.
sentences.zh: 总统要求进行调查是正确的。

sentences.en: You don't hear them say, hey, everything the president did was fine.
sentences.zh: 你听不到他们说，嘿，总统做的一切都很好。

sentences.en: There's no problem here.
sentences.zh: 这里没有问题。

sentences.en: And here's the reason why.
sentences.zh: 原因如下。

sentences.en: They prefer to attack his accusers.
sentences.zh: 他们更愿意攻击他的指控者。

sentences.en: And there's a parallel there, right, with what the Democrats were saying in the late 90s about the GOP and its obsession with Clinton.
sentences.zh: 这与民主党人在90年代末关于共和党及其对克林顿的执念的言论有相似之处，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, that's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全正确。

sentences.en: They didn't want to go around defending Clinton.
sentences.zh: 他们不想四处为克林顿辩护。

sentences.en: They didn't think that
sentences.zh: 他们不认为

sentences.en: Clinton was worth defending in the sense of what he had done.
sentences.zh: 克林顿所做的事值得为他辩护。

sentences.en: But they did want to attack the
sentences.zh: 但他们确实想攻击

sentences.en: Republicans by saying they had gone too far.
sentences.zh: 共和党人，称他们做得过头了。

sentences.en: The great story here for anybody willing to find it and write about it and explain it
sentences.zh: 对于任何愿意寻找、撰写和解释它的人来说，这里伟大的故事是

sentences.en: is this vast right-wing conspiracy that has been conspiring against my husband since the day he announced for president.
sentences.zh: 这个庞大的右翼阴谋集团，自我的丈夫宣布竞选总统之日起就一直在密谋反对他。

sentences.en: They had caved into the right-wing extremists of their party.
sentences.zh: 他们向党内的右翼极端分子屈服了。

sentences.en: They were obsessed with sex.
sentences.zh: 他们对性有着病态的执念。

sentences.en: And this was a wholly illegitimate effort.
sentences.zh: 这是一场完全非法的努力。

sentences.en: Mr. Speaker, Republicans, put your country before your party.
sentences.zh: 议长先生，共和党人，请把国家置于党派之上。

sentences.en: So while the subject matter of the two impeachments was starkly different, some of the tone and the rhetoric you're hearing, there is some parallel.
sentences.zh: 因此，虽然两次弹劾的主题截然不同，但你所听到的一些基调和修辞存在一些相似之处。

sentences.en: Peter, it strikes me that Nancy Pelosi and the Democrats had to have known all of this would be the case when they decided to move forward with the impeachment inquiry.
sentences.zh: 彼得，我感觉南希·佩洛西和民主党人在决定推进弹劾调查时，一定早就知道会是这样。

sentences.en: So why in their minds was it the right thing to do?
sentences.zh: 那么在他们看来，为什么这样做是正确的？

sentences.en: Yeah, it's a great question because up until now, Nancy Pelosi has not been interested in doing an impeachment.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一个很好的问题，因为在此之前，南希·佩洛西一直对进行弹劾不感兴趣。

sentences.en: She was there as a member of the Congress in 1998.
sentences.zh: 她在1998年时就是国会议员。

sentences.en: We are here today because the Republicans in the House are paralyzed with hatred of President
sentences.zh: 我们今天在这里，是因为众议院的共和党人被对克林顿总统的仇恨弄得瘫痪了

sentences.en: Clinton.
And until the Republicans free themselves of this hatred, our country will suffer.
sentences.zh: 除非共和党人摆脱这种仇恨，否则我们的国家将遭受痛苦。

sentences.en: Didn't think it worked out too well for the Republicans.
sentences.zh: 当时觉得这对共和党来说结果并不是很好。

sentences.en: Tonight on C-SPAN, Campaign 98 results.
sentences.zh: 今晚在C-SPAN频道，98年大选结果。

sentences.en: A party-line impeachment didn't help the Republicans at the polls in 1998.
sentences.zh: 党派色彩鲜明的弹劾在1998年的选举中对共和党没有任何帮助。

sentences.en: The Democrats had a much better day than anybody would have expected a few weeks ago.
sentences.zh: 民主党人度过了一个比几周前任何人的预期都要好得多的日子。

sentences.en: And also was seen by history as kind of somewhat less than a noble effort.
sentences.zh: 而且在历史上也被视为一种远谈不上崇高的努力。

sentences.en: And she didn't want the Democrats to be seen as just partisan attackers of Trump who can't get over their hatred of him so that they impeach him.
sentences.zh: 她不希望民主党人被视为仅仅是特朗普的党派攻击者，他们无法释怀对他的仇恨，因而对他进行弹劾。

sentences.en: But when this one came up, it just broke the dam.
sentences.zh: 但当这次事件出现时，它直接冲垮了堤坝。

sentences.en: It's just finally, OK, we've got to do something here.
sentences.zh: 终于，好吧，我们必须在这里做点什么了。

sentences.en: And I think that the speaker felt she had no choice but to move ahead.
sentences.zh: 我认为议长觉得她别无选择，只能继续推进。

sentences.en: But I guess what I mean is if the Democrats knew that impeachment basically never ends with a
sentences.zh: 但我想我的意思是，如果民主党人知道弹劾基本上从来不会以总统离职而告终，而特朗普会像尼克松那样自愿离职的想法

sentences.en: president leaving office and the idea that Trump would leave of his own volition like Nixon is
sentences.zh: 极其不可能，那么尽管存在民主党人所说的确凿证据，这次弹劾故事似乎更有可能重蹈克林顿的覆辙。

sentences.en: highly unlikely, then this impeachment story seems potentially more likely to go the way of Clinton despite the presence of what the Democrats are calling a smoking gun.
sentences.zh: 目前来看，确实如此。

sentences.en: At the moment, that's right.
sentences.zh: 但不同之处在于，尼克松和克林顿当时都处于他们的第二任期，对吧？

sentences.en: But the difference is that both Nixon and Clinton were in their second terms, right?
sentences.zh: 无论如何，他们最多也就再干几年。

sentences.en: They were not going to serve more than a couple more years no matter what.
sentences.zh: 这是我们第一次迎来一位处于第一任期的当选总统面临弹劾。

sentences.en: This is the first time we've had an elected president in his first term facing an impeachment.
sentences.zh: 因此，在这项决定做出后不久，选民将有机会做出决定，要么是因为总统仍在任，他们将决定是否让他继续留任，

sentences.en: So immediately after this decision, the voters will have a chance to decide either because the president will be there still and they will decide whether to keep him there
sentences.zh: 要么是因为他们决定将他赶下台，或者是因为他可能被免职，

sentences.en: or because they'll decide to throw him out or because maybe he will be removed from office
sentences.zh: 我们将迎来副总统彭斯作为共和党候选人站出来。

sentences.en: and we'll be having Vice President Pence standing up as the nominee for the Republican Party.
sentences.zh: 这里有很多不同的选择。

sentences.en: There's a lot of different options here.
sentences.zh: 但我认为我们确实看到了一些不同于以往任何一次我们见过的弹劾之争的事情。

sentences.en: But I think that really we're seeing something that's different than any previous impeachment battle that we've seen.
sentences.zh: 在比尔·克林顿的弹劾审判结束后，选民没有机会直接对他的去留进行投票。

sentences.en: Voters didn't get a chance to vote on Bill Clinton directly after his impeachment trial.
sentences.zh: 他们根本没有机会对理查德·尼克松进行投票。

sentences.en: They didn't get a chance to vote on Richard Nixon at all.
sentences.zh: 安德鲁·约翰逊甚至没有获得他所在政党的提名，因此他在弹劾审判后没有参选。

sentences.en: Andrew Johnson didn't even get his party nomination, so he didn't run after his impeachment trial.
sentences.zh: 所以这是第一次，假设特朗普总统没有离职，选民将在弹劾和审判（假设它们发生）之后不久对一位总统做出裁决。

sentences.en: So this is the first time, assuming President Trump doesn't leave office, that voters will
sentences.zh: 因此我认为，我们已经改变了我们在未来13个月里即将进行的对话。

sentences.en: render a judgment on a president shortly after an impeachment and a trial, assuming they happen.
sentences.zh: 彼得，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: And so I think we have transformed the conversation that we're about to have for the next 13 months.
sentences.zh: 彼得，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: Peter, thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 彼得，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: The Times reports that President Trump pressured another foreign leader for a political favor in recent weeks.
sentences.zh: 《泰晤士报》报道称，特朗普总统最近几周向另一位外国领导人施压，以谋求政治利益。

sentences.en: During a phone call with the Prime Minister of Australia,
sentences.zh: 在与澳大利亚总理的通话中，

sentences.en: Trump pushed for help to discredit the special counsel's Russia investigation.
sentences.zh: 特朗普施压对方协助抹黑特别检察官对俄罗斯的调查。

sentences.en: Afterward, the White House restricted access to records of the call, just as it did to the transcript of the president's July call to the leader of Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 事后，白宫限制了查阅通话记录的权限，就像对待总统7月份与乌克兰领导人通话的文字记录一样。

sentences.en: On Monday, House Democrats issued their second subpoena related to that call, this time to the president's personal lawyer, Rudy Giuliani,
sentences.zh: 周一，众议院民主党人发出了与该次通话有关的第二张传票，对象是总统的私人律师鲁迪·朱利安尼，

sentences.en: seeking his private communications with the president.
sentences.zh: 要求获取他与总统的私人通信。

sentences.en: Mr. President, do you now know who the whistleblower is, sir?
sentences.zh: 总统先生，您现在知道举报人是谁了吗，先生？

sentences.en: Well, we're trying to find out about a whistleblower.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们正在试图了解举报人的情况。

sentences.en: We have a whistleblower that reports things that were incorrect.
sentences.zh: 我们有一个举报人，他举报的内容并不属实。

sentences.en: At the White House, President Trump said he was eager to identify the whistleblower, despite legal protections specifically designed to keep the whistleblower anonymous.
sentences.zh: 在白宫，特朗普总统表示他急于查明举报人的身份，尽管有专门旨在保持举报人匿名身份的法律保护。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要知道的其他消息。

sentences.en: On Monday, California's governor, Gavin Newsom, signed a law allowing college athletes at public and private universities to sign endorsement deals with major companies.
sentences.zh: 周一，加州州长加文·纽森签署了一项法律，允许公立和私立大学的运动员与各大公司签署代言协议。

sentences.en: A decision that could ultimately transform the economics of college sports.
sentences.zh: 这一决定最终可能会改变大学体育的经济格局。

sentences.en: Billions and billions of dollars, 14-plus billion dollars goes to these universities, goes to these colleges, billion-plus revenue to the NCAA themselves.
sentences.zh: 数以百亿计的美元，超过140亿美元流入了这些大学，流入了这些高校，NCAA自身也有十多亿美元的收入。

sentences.en: And the actual product, the folks that are putting their lives on the line, putting everything on the line, are getting nothing.
sentences.zh: 而真正的主角，那些把生命押上、把一切都押上的人，却什么也没得到。

sentences.en: Under current rules, such deals are prohibited.
sentences.zh: 根据现行规则，此类交易是被禁止的。

sentences.en: A system that has allowed universities and TV networks to profit from college sports, but prevented the athletes themselves from earning money.
sentences.zh: 这样一个系统让大学和电视网络从大学体育中牟取暴利，却阻碍了运动员自己赚钱。

sentences.en: It's going to initiate dozens of other states to introduce similar legislation.
sentences.zh: 这将引发其他几十个州也出台类似立法。

sentences.en: And it's going to change college sports for the better by having now the interests, finally, of the athletes on par with the interests of the institutions.
sentences.zh: 它将让运动员的利益终于与机构的利益平起平坐，从而朝着更好的方向改变大学体育。

sentences.en: Now we're rebalancing that power arrangement.
sentences.zh: 现在我们正在重新平衡这种权力结构。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是本期《每日简报》。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Babarro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个受严密控制的机器运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 当时选举迎来了一群自称改革派的人士。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 自那以后，该党便陷入了一场残酷、混乱、有时又激动人心的争斗之中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在最新一期的《都市》播客中，由我萨拉·凯尼格为您讲述人们试图维持影响力却在过程中逐渐失控的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 《都市》。

sentences.en: Listen wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 请在各大播客平台收听。
